name: Peter Mandelson
role: British Labour politician: cabinet minister, EU Trade Commissioner (2004-2008), Business Secretary (2008-2010), UK ambassador to the US (2025)
summary: Architect of New Labour's modernisation, he combined acceptance of markets, private enterprise and low redistribution with an activist role for government in industry and innovation. He is a consistent pro-EU, pro-trade voice who opposed Brexit and backed a vote on the final deal. Many specific positions on social and foreign policy are not recorded.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Mixed: endorsed 'markets wherever possible, government intervention wherever necessary' (2008) but in 2009 said there was too much of a mindset that markets are best left to operate freely.

public-ownership.rationale: The Blair Revolution, per reviewer, treated privatisation as a success and social ownership as outdated; as Business Secretary sought a part-sale of Royal Mail.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: 1998: 'intensely relaxed about people becoming filthy rich ... as long as they pay their taxes'; The Blair Revolution (per reviewer) ruled out redistributive rates, citing need for incentives; in 2015 called Labour's mansion tax 'crude and short-termist'.

free-trade.rationale: Pursued the Doha round as EU Trade Commissioner and, as ambassador, said he would negotiate tariffs down further; also cautioned that liberalisation is not 'a panacea for development'.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: As Trade Commissioner resisted French calls to extend Chinese textile quotas and warned against protectionism; as ambassador sought lower tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Said government has an 'essential role' in innovation and growth sectors, but not a dominant one; did not endorse state direction of investment as such.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: In 2009 opposed cutting spending during the recession and wanted stimulus kept until recovery was secure, with debt reduced by a credible plan.

force-without-un.rationale: No stated general position on force without UN approval; his remarks on a second Iraq resolution are something nearby.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Blair Revolution (per reviewer) backed workfare for the long-term unemployed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Book (per reviewer) would keep Conservative-era union laws including limits on secondary action.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Long-standing pro-EU voice, EU Commissioner, sat on the Remain campaign board and opposed Brexit; no quote on 'pooling sovereignty' itself.

common-currency.rationale: No stated position found; a press description of him as pro-euro is not his own words.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Blair Revolution (per reviewer) supported stripping hereditary peers of their vote.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Blair Revolution (per reviewer) backed a public right to know underwritten by legislation, with exemptions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Favoured 'further individualisation of our public services' with parent and patient choice; book (per reviewer) favoured competitive tendering and private-sector models.

social-market-economy.rationale: Endorsed markets wherever possible with government intervention where necessary, and opposed Conservative cuts to frontline services.

abolish-ip.rationale: As Business Secretary drove copyright enforcement, including a graduated response that could end in disconnection of persistent infringers.

second-chamber.rationale: Book (per reviewer) kept a second chamber, suggesting it might become more representative.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Book (per reviewer) expressed scepticism towards universal benefits; evidence concerns benefits, not all social spending.

notes: Appointed ambassador Dec 2024, took up post Feb 2025, dismissed by Starmer 11 Sep 2025 over Epstein links; arrested Feb 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office. None of this is used as evidence of ideology. Full texts of The Blair Revolution and The Third Man were not available online; book positions come from reviews and are capped at medium. Hansard and europa.eu speech archives were not reachable via search; several pages (taxresearch Guardian letter, gov.uk, BusinessGreen, Computing, committees.parliament.uk, RSA, Express and Star, Cato) returned 403/429.
